m:
Kocaeli Province (Turkish: Kocaeli ili, pronounced [koˈdʒaeli]) is a province and metropolitan municipality of Turkey and one of only three not to have the same official name as its capital, İzmit, which is thus also sometimes called Kocaeli. Its area is 3,397 km2 (1,312 sq mi), and its population is 2,102,907 (2023). The province is the successor of the Ottoman-era Sanjak of Kocaeli. The largest towns in the province are İzmit and Gebze. The traffic code is 41.
The province is located at the easternmost end of the Sea of Marmara around the Gulf of İzmit. Kocaeli is bordered by the province of Istanbul and the Marmara Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north, the province of Sakarya to the east, the province of Bursa to the south and the province of Yalova to the southwest. The metropolitan area of Istanbul extends to the Kocaeli-Istanbul provincial border. 
The size and natural conditions of the Bay of İzmit allow for extensive port facilities, including the Gölcük Naval Base. The province is called the industrial capital of Turkey. Kocaeli has an airport named Cengiz Topel Naval Air Station which is used for military and civilian transport. Kocaeli has three universities: Kocaeli University, Gebze Technical University and Kocaeli Health and Technology University.

Q28197519:
Kocaeli Museum, a.k.a. Kocaeli Archaeology and Ethnography Museum or İzmit Museum, (Turkish: Kocaeli Müzesi) is a national museum in Kocaeli (İzmit), northwestern Turkey, exhibiting archaeological artifacts and ethnographic objects. It is housed in the former railway station of İzmit.
The museum is situated on İstasyon St. in Kozlu neighborhood of İzmit.
The railway station was designed by German architect Otto Ritter, and built between 1873 and 1910. The facility covers an area of 21 daa (5.2 acres). The railway station became defunct after the course of the railway, which ran along the coast of Marmara Sea and passed through the city center, was changed to run north of the city.
After restoration works for redevelopment, which began in 2004, the former railway station was opened early 2007. The museum consists of 1,965 archaeological, 1,549 ethnographic objects and 5,155 coins. In addition to the exhibition halls, there is a 130-seated conference room and a laboratory. The museum objects are partly exhibited in the museum halls and partly open-air in the museum yard. A steam locomotive and two railroad cars, redesigned as cafeteria and restaurant and situated in front of the museum, serve the visitors.
In the museum halls, artifacts from Paleolithic, Hellenic, Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman era are exhibited.
Q65220544: Seka Park in İzmit was created on the site of the former Seka paper mill. It lies in the city centre on the shore of the Gulf of İzmit, beside the D-100 highway.
Q105340772: Ormanya, full name Ormanya Natural Life Park, is a wildlife park in the Kartepe district of Kocaeli.
Q4198699:
Gulf of İzmit (Turkish: İzmit körfezi), also referred to as İzmit Bay, is a bay at the easternmost edge of the Sea of Marmara, in Kocaeli Province, Turkey. The gulf takes its name from the city of İzmit. Other cities and towns around the bay are Gebze, Körfez, Gölcük, and Altınova.
In the east–west direction, it extends for a length of about 48 kilometres (30 mi), while in the north–south direction its width varies from 2 to 3 kilometres (1.2 to 1.9 mi) at the narrowest spots to about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) at its widest. The İzmit Bay Bridge is a suspension bridge that bridges the gulf.
The North Anatolian Fault Zone, the most prominent active fault in Turkey and the source of numerous large earthquakes throughout history, passes through the Gulf of İzmit.
Q25338950:
The Osman Gazi Bridge (Turkish: Osmangazi Köprüsü) is a suspension bridge spanning the Gulf of İzmit at its narrowest point, 2,620 m (8,600 ft). The bridge links the Turkish city of Gebze to the Yalova Province and carries the O-5 motorway across the gulf.
The bridge was opened on 1 July 2016 to become the then-longest suspension bridge in Turkey and the fourth-longest (ninth-longest as of 2025) suspension bridge in the world by the length of its central span.
The length of the bridge was surpassed by the Çanakkale 1915 Bridge across the Dardanelles strait, which became the longest suspension bridge in the world when it was opened on 18 March 2022.
Q6047559:
Kefken Island (Turkish: Kefken Adası), lies off the Black Sea coast of Turkey, a short boat ride from the mainland village of Cebeci in the Kandıra district of Kocaeli Province.
It has an area of 21 hectares, and is about four times as long as it is broad.
Q8080275:
The İzmit Clock Tower (Turkish: İzmit Saat Kulesi) in İzmit, Turkey is one of many clock towers that were built throughout the Ottoman Empire as a result of the decree which was sent to the provincial governors to commemorate the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdülhamid II's ascension to the Ottoman throne. It was designed by architect Vedat Tek upon the order of Musa Kazım Bey, the governor of İzmit, and built in 1902. Other sources name the architect of the tower as Mihran Azaryan who was an Armenian-Ottoman of Izmit origin.
The neoclassical clock tower, which stands just in front of the Hünkar Pavilion of Sultan Abdülaziz, has four floors with dimensions 3.65 m × 3.65 m (12.0 ft × 12.0 ft). The ground floor houses fountains, while the clock is on the top floor. All four facades of the middle floors are decorated with the seal of Sultan Abdülhamid II. The pointed cone on top is coated with lead. 
The clock tower has been an inseparable part of the history of İzmit throughout the 20th century, and has become the symbol of the city.
In the former Balkan provinces of the Ottoman Empire, particularly in present-day Serbian, Bosnian and Montenegrin towns such as Belgrade, Prijepolje, Sarajevo, Banja Luka, Gradačac and Stara Varoš, similar Ottoman era clock towers are still named Sahat Kula (deriving from the Turkish words Saat Kulesi, meaning Clock Tower.)
It was restored in 2006.
Q18209673: The Pertev Mehmet Paşa Mosque (Turkish: Pertev Paşa Camii), also known as Yeni Cuma Cami (lit. 'New Friday Mosque'), is a mosque located in the town of Izmit, in the province of Kocaeli, Turkey.
Q6872777: Bahçecik is an area of the Başiskele district of Kocaeli, south of the Gulf of İzmit at the foot of the Samanlı Mountains. Until the early 20th century its population was mostly Armenian.
Q6083171: The Hannibal Monument was built in 1981 in memory of Hannibal on Hannibal Hill, within the TÜBİTAK grounds in Gebze.
Q5073952:
Charax in Bithynia was a Roman and Byzantine port town of ancient Bithynia, in what is now Turkey. It was on the north side of the Sinus Astacenus on the road between the erstwhile Eastern Roman and Byzantine capital Nicomedia and Libyssa. Stephanus of Byzantium calls it a place of great trade.
Its site is located near Hereke, in Asiatic Turkey.
Q25475745: The Çoban Mustafa Pasha Complex is a 16th-century Ottoman complex on Bağdat Street, Şeftali Sokak, in central Gebze, Kocaeli. It is thought, though not certain, to be the work of Mimar Sinan.
Q104519818: Fevziye Mosque in İzmit, Kocaeli, was first built in the 16th century and is a listed heritage building.
Q104669707: Selim Sırrı Pasha Mansion is in İzmit, the centre of Kocaeli. Built by Selim Sırrı Pasha, district governor of İzmit, it was completed in 1892. The timber and masonry house has two floors and an attic; ancient Roman stones are built into its garden walls, and the interior has hand-painted decoration.
Q30623231:
Uzunkum Nature Park (Turkish: Uzunkum Tabiat Parkı) is a nature park declared coastal area in Kocaeli Province, northwestern Turkey.
Uzunkum, literally long sandy beach, is located at Black Sea east of Cebeci village in Kandıra district of Kocaeli Province. The area was declared a nature park by the Ministry of Environment and Forest in 2014. The nature park consists of the parts, the sandy beach in the north and forested hillside. It covers an area of 235 ha (580 acres).
The nature park offers outdoor recreational activities like hiking, swimming, surfing and angling.
Flora
The vegetation of the nature park consists of the endangered sea daffodil (Pancratium maritimum), Syrian juniper (Juniperus drupacea), juniper, Valonia oak (Quercus macrolepis), laurel (Laurus nobilis), oak, hornbeam (Carpinus), common ash (Fraxinus excelsior), cedar (Cedrus), cypress, willow, rose hip, buxus, European cornel (Cornus mas), spurge (Cornus mas), Cercis, pilewort, Crocus, trefoil (Trifolium), hemp and diverse algae species.
Fauna
The nature is habitat for the mammals fox, jackal, hare, beaver, badger, crested porcupine, the reptile tortoise, the bird species woodcock, quail, gull, black cormorant, francolin, partridge, common blackbird, kingfisher and owl.
Q102316131: Kefkenada Lighthouse is a lighthouse on Kefken Island in the Kandıra district of Kocaeli.
Q49371580: Yuvacık is an area of the Başiskele district of Kocaeli.
Q3696280: Değirmendere is a neighbourhood of Gölcük, Kocaeli. Formerly a town with its own municipality, it was merged into Gölcük in 2008.
Q106823698: Orhan Mosque (Gazi Süleyman Pasha Mosque) is a 14th-century Ottoman mosque in the Orhan quarter of İzmit.
Q106823712: Yumurtacı Mosque was built in 1631 on Hacı Hasan Sırrı Paşa Street in İzmit, Kocaeli, by Yumurtacı Muhammet Ali Ağa, who is buried there. The rectangular mud-brick mosque has survived to this day through several repairs and is noted for having come through natural disasters undamaged.
Q65045318:
Arbeila was a town of ancient Bithynia on the coast of the Sinus Astacenus west of Nicomedia. Its name does not appear in ancient authors but is inferred from epigraphic and other evidence.
Its site is located near Tuzla, in Asiatic Turkey.
Q106619418: The Akça Koca Bey Mausoleum is the tomb of Akça Koca Bey in Babaköy, in the Kandıra district of Kocaeli.
Q106727518: Portakal Hafız Mansion is a mansion in İzmit, the centre of Kocaeli.
Q106858944: Hereke Castle is in the Körfez district of Kocaeli and is thought to have been built in the 640s, in the Roman (Byzantine) period.
Q108680788: The Kaiser Wilhelm II Pavilion, also called the Nail-less Pavilion, is in the Körfez district of Kocaeli. It was built in 1898 for the visit of the German Emperor Wilhelm II to the Ottoman Empire.
Q114742350: Eskihisar Castle is a historic fortress in the Eskihisar quarter of Gebze, Kocaeli. It was built on a steep hill north-east of Eskihisar village to control the crossing south of the Gulf of İzmit and protect the harbour, and is thought to date from the Byzantine period.
Q131738681: Çoban Mustafa Pasha Bath is a hamam in Gebze. It belongs to the complex built by Çoban Mustafa Pasha, completed between 1522 and 1524. It is a symmetrical double bath in classical Ottoman style, built of rubble stone and brick.
Q107751521: Saatçi Ali Efendi Mansion was built in 1774, in the reign of Abdulhamid I, on a sloping street overlooking the sea in İzmit, Kocaeli. One of the oldest surviving mansions in the city, it stands on Alaca Mescit Yokuşu in the Veli Ahmet quarter, 250 metres from the centre.
Q6009286: The Abdulaziz Hunting Lodge, or Kasr-ı Hümayun, is a baroque and Empire-style pavilion in İzmit. It took its final form under Sultan Abdulaziz and is known as the only small palace the Ottomans built outside Istanbul. Designed by Garabet Amira Balyan, it is now a museum.
Q106624186: The İzmit Earthquake Remembrance and Awareness Museum is an earthquake museum in the İzmit district of Kocaeli.
İzmit Deprem Anma ve Farkındalık Müzesi
Q106858914: The Osman Hamdi Bey Museum has been open since 1987 in the two-storey house in Eskihisar, Gebze (Kocaeli), where Osman Hamdi Bey spent his summers in the last years of his life.
Q108802041: Servetiye Museum in the Başiskele district of Kocaeli was built in 2012, led by Kocaeli Metropolitan Municipality with help from Başiskele Municipality and District Governorate. It displays weapons and tools from the War of Independence, local cultural objects and written and visual material from the war, labelled with the names of their donors.
Q6027918: Ballıkayalar is a rocky canyon valley near the village of Tavşanlı in Gebze, Kocaeli, protected as a nature park.
Q31189359: Kuzuyayla Nature Park is in the Kartepe district of Kocaeli. Declared a park in 2011, it has rich vegetation and views of Lake Sapanca.
Q34929634: Tahtalı Pond in the Tahtalı quarter of Derince, Kocaeli, is one of the largest ponds (small reservoirs) in Türkiye.
Q106889487: Harikalar Sahili is an award-winning seafront at the 60 Evler shore in the Derince district of Kocaeli. Derince Municipality began building it in 2005, and it officially opened in 2007.
Q20988515: IT Valley (Turkish: Bilişim Vadisi), formerly known as Silicon Valley of Turkey (Turkish: Türkiye'nin Silikon Vadisi) was a proposed project of Turkish architect Günay Erdem and Turkish landscape architect Sunay Erdem for the Turkish version of the Silicon Valley at San Francisco, United States.
Q125463552: Kartepe Cable Car is a gondola lift in the Kartepe district of Kocaeli, the province's first cable car line.
Q131403316: Servetiye Bridge is a stone bridge in the Servetiye Karşı quarter of Başiskele, Kocaeli. Its building technique and materials resemble the stone bridges of the eastern Black Sea.
Q119443098: Canfeda Kethüda Hatun Fountain is a 16th-century fountain opposite Orhan Mosque in the Orhan quarter of İzmit, Kocaeli.
Q118955894: The Kocaeli Press Museum in İzmit displays old issues of local newspapers, old cameras, printing tools and old typewriters. It opened on 16 January 2014 with support from the Turkish Journalists' Federation and İzmit Municipality.
Q140389754: The Serindere Waterfalls are six separate falls in the Serindere Canyon, which runs between the Başiskele and Kartepe districts of Kocaeli.
Q106889431: Bağırganlı Beach, also called Taflan Bay, is a free Blue Flag beach 550 metres long and 100 metres wide, 17 km from Kandıra town in Kocaeli. One of the largest beaches on the Black Sea coast, it is the area's most popular beach in summer, with many hotels and guesthouses nearby.
Q106889452: Kerpe Beach is one of the Blue Flag beaches of the Kandıra district of Kocaeli. It is 500 metres long and 10 metres wide, with toilets, parking, bicycle parking, shade, changing cabins, lifeguards and first aid, showers, sunbathing areas, a safe swimming zone and facilities for disabled visitors.
Q106889464: Cebeci Beach is a Blue Flag beach in the Kandıra district of Kocaeli, with Tuzağzı Nature Park to the north-east and the pink rocks to the south-west. The 5–6 km beach has very clean water and a wide stretch of fine sand; a barchan dune lies in the dunes west of Cebeci village.
Q106730213: Gölkay Park is an amusement park in İzmit, Kocaeli.
